headline: The rally has support: foreign funds bought for a 12th straight day and Asia is up this morning. But Nifty is just under **26,000**, a level option sellers are defending hard, so a quiet or capped day is likely.

mood.label: Positive
mood.why: Three of the dashboard's four direction checks point up (bias score +45), but the option chain points the other way. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: Overnight: US stock futures are up about **1–2%** since India closed, and Korea is up 2.8%. Both help the open.
Brent crude is up **1.1%** to $96 after reported Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites. Costlier oil hurts India, which buys most of its oil abroad.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought **₹5,843 crore** of Indian shares yesterday, their 12th buying day in a row. Domestic funds bought ₹5,631 crore too.
My call: the rally more likely **continues, slowly**, than reverses. The likely limit is 26,000, where traders have sold the most bets on a rise.
Fear is still fairly high for a rising market. India VIX is 16.8, higher than on 75% of days in the past year.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night was mostly good for the open, and it supports yesterday's small rise, but oil rose and GIFT Nifty points to only a flat start.

points.text: GIFT Nifty, which trades overnight and hints at the open, was around **25,985–25,990** early today. Reports disagree on whether it is slightly up or down, so expect a roughly flat start.
US markets were shut for Thanksgiving. US futures still rose: S&P 500 up **1.0%** and Nasdaq up 1.9% since India's close, as tech shares bounced after weeks of losses.
Asia is up: Korea **+2.8%**, Japan +1.2%, Hong Kong and Taiwan +0.5%. China is flat.
Brent is up **1.1%** and gold up 2%. The US 10-year bond rate rose 0.04 points to 4.91%. Higher US rates make US bonds more attractive to the same foreign money that is buying India.
Dollar and rupee were flat. US-listed Infosys and Wipro last traded on Wednesday, so they add **no new signal** today.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: Yesterday was a small up day (+0.25%). I expect slow continuation rather than a pullback, with low-to-medium confidence.

points.text: For continuation: FIIs are buying heavily in cash shares (a **₹1.28 lakh crore** net purchase this month), and futures traders added fresh bets on a rise (futures open positions up 4.1% with price up).
FIIs still hold mostly bets on a fall in index futures (only **23%** long). If the market keeps rising, they may have to buy back those bets in a hurry, which can push prices higher.
For a pullback: Nifty is up about **14%** in about four weeks and sits 9% above its 50-day average. Moves that fast often pause.
Option sellers added large bets against a rise at **26,000** and 26,100 yesterday. That level has stopped the market before.
What would prove me wrong: a close below **25,700**, or FIIs turning to net sellers.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is clearly up, but the option market expects a ceiling near 26,000.

points.text: Nifty at 25,885 is above its 20, 50 and 200-day averages, with **higher highs and higher lows**. That gives the trend check its top score (+2).
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) rose from 0.94 to **1.09** in five sessions. More traders are selling protection below the market, a sign of confidence.
Weighted by who actually traded, option flows lean **negative** (score −0.63), mainly from new call selling at 26,000–26,400.
The overall bias score is **+45** (bullish), with 3 of 4 checks agreeing. That is medium conviction.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Both foreign and Indian funds are buying shares, but foreigners are still hedged against a fall.

points.text: FIIs bought a net **₹5,843 crore** yesterday, a big day by the dashboard's rule (over ₹3,000 crore).
Domestic funds (DIIs) bought **₹5,631 crore** as well. When both buy, there is less selling pressure.
Reports say FIIs are moving money from crowded AI-linked markets like Korea and Taiwan to India, expecting **better company earnings**. That is a reason the buying could last.

In index futures, FIIs added about **3,200** more net bets on a fall yesterday. But they also cut their net put options (another kind of bet on a fall) by about 55,000 contracts. These signals cut both ways.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Global markets are calmer this week, but high US interest rates and oil remain the main risks.

points.text: Short-term US bond rates suggest markets expect the **Fed to raise rates** in December. That would pull money back to the US.
Brent is still down **17%** over the past month, even after this week's jump. Over that period, oil has helped India.
The rupee is about **2.9%** stronger against the dollar than a month ago, which helps foreign investors' returns.
The US fear gauge (VIX) eased to 26.8 but is still high. US stocks are down **7%** in a month.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No Nifty 50 company reported this week, so results won't move the index today.

points.text: Siemens Energy India reported revenue up **30%** and profit up 81% on last year: a Strong result by the dashboard's rule.
The other filings were small companies, several of them **loss-making**. None of them matters for Nifty.
IT shares are the market's leaders. Nifty IT rose about **7%** in four sessions, with HCL Tech the top gainer yesterday.
No big-company results are due in the next week.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Next week is busy: GDP, an expiry, and the RBI decision.

points.text: **Monday 30 Nov, 4 pm:** India's GDP for July–September. A big surprise either way can move the whole market.
**Tuesday 1 Dec:** weekly options expiry. With 26,000 heavily defended, the index can swing sharply near the close.
**Friday 4 Dec, 10 am:** RBI rate decision. It matters most for banks, which are about 30% of FII holdings.
**10 Dec:** the Fed decision. A rate rise is widely expected, and a tougher message could slow foreign buying.
More attacks on Saudi oil sites could push oil higher. That would be the **fastest way** for this read to go wrong.

levels.note: A close above 26,000 would mean call sellers have given way and could speed up the rally. A close below 25,500 would break the main support and signal the rally is cracking.

watch.text: The open versus GIFT Nifty near 25,985. A flat start is expected.
Whether Nifty can trade above 26,000, or keeps getting pushed back from it.
Brent crude near $96: any new reports of attacks on Saudi oil sites.
Provisional FII/DII figures. The question is whether the 12-day buying streak survives.
US markets close early (1 pm New York) after Thanksgiving. Watch whether the tech bounce holds.

bottom_line: The trend, money flows and futures data all point up, and overnight news is mostly supportive. The dashboard reads a bullish bias of +45 with medium conviction. My read is a slow push higher rather than a reversal, but 26,000 is a strong ceiling with expiry four days away, so the day may stay in a tight range. The main risk is oil: more attacks on Saudi supply could undo the good news from abroad.
